question: Should OpenClaw accept SourceActor as the public generic SDK/prompt attribution contract for channel message authors?
rationale: The implementation is additive, but plugin SDK exports and prompt context fields become durable public API; automation cannot choose whether this should be the canonical contract versus keeping attribution in channelContext or deferring to the memory design.

options.title: Accept SourceActor contract
options.body: Land the prerequisite stack, fix the hook docs mismatch, and treat SourceActor plus scalar mirrors as the supported additive attribution shape.

options.title: Keep attribution hook-local
options.body: Remove or narrow the public SourceActor prompt/SDK surface and keep richer identity under existing channelContext-style hook metadata for now.

options.title: Defer to memory design
options.body: Pause this PR until the memory attribution follow-up settles whether the same shape is sufficient for recall and persistence boundaries.

recommendation.title: Accept SourceActor contract
recommendation.body: Land the prerequisite stack, fix the hook docs mismatch, and treat SourceActor plus scalar mirrors as the supported additive attribution shape.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest recent history across inbound context, plugin SDK surface, and public contract refactors involved in this choice.
